title: FAA Airworthiness Directive 2024-09-15: Wing Spar Inspection for Boeing 737-800 and 737-900ER
content:
The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Boeing Model 737-800 and 737-900ER series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of fatigue cracking found in the wing front spar lower chord at Wing Buttock Line (WBL) 160 during scheduled maintenance.

AD NUMBER: 2024-09-15
EFFECTIVE DATE: May 22, 2024

APPLICABILITY:
- Boeing 737-800 series, line numbers 3200 through 5400
- Boeing 737-900ER series, line numbers 3800 through 4200
- As identified in Boeing Service Bulletin 737-57-1362, dated March 2024

COMPLIANCE REQUIRED:
1. Initial inspection: Within 18 months or 6,000 flight cycles after the effective date, whichever occurs first.
2. Inspection method: Detailed visual inspection (DVI) and high-frequency eddy current (HFEC) inspection of the wing front spar lower chord at WBL 160, left and right wings.
3. Repetitive inspections: Every 3,000 flight cycles after initial inspection.
4. If cracking is found: Repair using Boeing-approved repair method within 30 flight cycles of discovery. Contact Boeing for repair data.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS OF COMPLIANCE (AMOC):
Requests for AMOCs must be submitted to the Manager, Seattle ACO Branch, FAA, at sean.williams@faa.gov or (206) 231-3500.

COST ESTIMATE:
- Number of affected airplanes: approximately 1,200 worldwide
- Cost per inspection: $2,850 (8 work-hours at $85/hour plus materials)
- Total fleet cost for initial inspection: $3,420,000

REFERENCED SERVICE BULLETIN: Boeing Service Bulletin 737-57-1362, dated March 14, 2024

This AD is issued under authority of 49 U.S.C. 44701(a).
